tasks.goal: Assess tape-out readiness for an RF digital-to-analog converter from its spectral and performance data.
tasks.prompt:
Write a tape-out readiness analysis and recommendation for the radio-frequency digital-to-analog converter (RF-DAC) as your response text, not as an attached file. Use the attached architecture block diagram, input and output spectrum plots, and sign-off performance limits chart. In this report, in-band means 0 Hz to 16 GHz, and every reported quantity takes one committed value.

Structure the report as follows:

Section 0: Architecture: Name each external input signal and each external output signal of the converter, and state the function of each.

Section 1: Spectral Analysis: List the frequency and level of each output-spectrum tone needed to calculate the tape-out gating specifications. Classify each marked output-spectrum tone by architectural origin as fundamental, harmonic distortion (state the order), time-interleaving spur, DAC Nyquist image, clock feedthrough, or no architectural origin, and give the percentage of marked output-spectrum tones that have an architectural origin. State the frequency of the worst-case DAC Nyquist image, and state which marked tone is the worst-case time-interleaving spur together with its level relative to the fundamental in dBc and how many dB it lies above the other time-interleaving spur. Give the total harmonic distortion (THD) of the marked harmonic-distortion tones, as their power sum relative to the fundamental in dBc. Finally, state the two most dominant mechanisms attenuating the in-band noise floor of the output spectrum.

Section 2: Calculations: Detail the formulas and arithmetic for each tape-out gating specification, and only those specifications.

Section 3: Results: Provide a PASS / FAIL table with exactly one row per tape-out gating specification, each row containing the specification name, measured value, margin, and PASS / FAIL, followed by the percentage of tape-out gating specifications that passed and the passing gating specifications listed in order of decreasing margin.

Section 4: Conclusion: Give a tape-out recommendation of APPROVED or REJECTED that identifies each violation and the amount by which it exceeds its limit.

Format all tone frequencies, levels, percentages, and dB and dBc values in Section 1, all calculated results in Section 2, and all Section 3 values to two decimal places. Write the document title and all section titles in uppercase. Separate major sections with exactly two blank lines. Number the sections, use hyphen bullets for all other lists, and indent sub-bullets by exactly two spaces per level. Do not use asterisks anywhere in the response. Render the Section 3 table in monospaced text so that cells on different lines line up vertically.

tasks.goal: Analyze zinc-binding assay data for a mutant protein series and present the results in a PowerPoint deck.
tasks.input_files: Branding_Layout.pptx, PPT_File.pptx, Paper_1.pdf, Paper_2.pdf, Paper_3.pdf, Zinc_binding_values.xlsx
tasks.prompt:
Construct a PPTX file (titled Zinc_Binding_Assay.pptx) using the branding layout that includes -
Slide 1: An introduction slide for the zinc-binding assay (ZBA). Heading: "Zinc binding assay". Provide assay workflow and APA citation for Paper 2. Draw chemical structures to show reversible absorbance shift from PAR (4-(2-pyridylazo)resorcinol) (416nm) to (PAR)2·ZN(II).
Slide 2: Create a solid line graph plotting Zn/protein monomer versus PMB (p-hydroxymercuribenzoate) Equivalents (relative to hexameric protein) for a hexameric protein (concentration of the hexameric protein: 5 µM) for WT (wild-type), R0S, R1S, R1,2S mutants using the absorbance values provided in the zinc binding file. The absorbance values for the standard zinc graph are also provided (linear regression). Round off all values to 4 decimal places. Calculate Zn/protein monomer for all the proteins (baseline correction with respect to 0 µM PMB should be done after calculating zinc concentration and before calculating zinc concentration/ protein monomer). Heading: "Zinc Binding Is Altered in Mutants". The mutants indicate that the amino acid R is mutated to S.
Slide 3: Label the individual components of the 2D classifications of protein structure with provided arrow. Also, list the orientation of the components in panels 1,2,4,5,8.  Provide orientation examples, where n = #:side view of ClpPn, ClpPn views, single-capped ClpXP particle, double-capped ClpXP particle, ClpXn.

Short cells (<5µm), long filamentous cells (5-10µm), and very long filamentous cells (>10µm). Heading: Comparative studies of filamentation defects. Italicise mutant names.

States the equation of motion for the system on the "System Model" slide as \(m\ddot{x} + C(x)\dot{x} + K(x) = F\). Algebraically equivalent equation-of-motion notations are acceptable, such as \(m\ddot{x} + C(x, \dot{x}) + K(x, \dot{x}) = F(t)\), and \(m\ddot{x} + c\dot{x} + C(x, \dot{x}) + K(x, \dot{x}) = F(t)\).

States that the restoring force is zero in the clearance subspace on the “Backlash Nonlinearity” slide. Equivalent force symbols and argument lists, such as $K(x)$, $K(x,\dot{x})$ or $F_s$, are acceptable. Equivalent subspace descriptions include $x \in V$, $(x,\dot{x}) \in V$, and alternative region labels or conditions that denote the same clearance subspace as $V$.

States the restoring forces as $k_1(x+b)$ in the left contact subspace $V_1$ and $k_2(x-b)$ in the right contact subspace $V_2$ on the “Backlash Nonlinearity” slide. Algebraically equivalent force laws, alternative force symbols and argument lists, and equivalent subspace descriptions are acceptable. These descriptions include phase space membership $(x,\dot{x}) \in V_1$ and $(x,\dot{x}) \in V_2$, and alternative region labels or conditions that denote the same left and right contact subspaces as $V_1$ and $V_2$, respectively.

States either the total damping force $c\dot{x}$ or a contact-damping contribution of zero in the clearance subspace $V$ on the “Backlash Nonlinearity” slide. The zero-contact-damping form, such as $C(x)=0$ or $C(x,\dot{x})=0$, is acceptable when the permanent base damping $c\dot{x}$ is included separately in the equation of motion on the “System Model” slide or on the “Backlash Nonlinearity” slide. The resulting force balance includes the base damping contribution exactly once. Equivalent force or damping-coefficient notation and equivalent subspace descriptions, including $x \in V$, $(x,\dot{x}) \in V$, or alternative labels identifying the same clearance subspace, are acceptable.

States the damping contributions in the contact subspaces on the “Backlash Nonlinearity” slide using either total damping forces $(c+c_1)\dot{x}$ in the left contact subspace $V_1$ and $(c+c_2)\dot{x}$ in the right contact subspace $V_2$, or contact damping forces $c_1\dot{x}$ in $V_1$ and $c_2\dot{x}$ in $V_2$, with the permanent base damping $c\dot{x}$ included separately in the equation of motion on the “System Model” slide or on the “Backlash Nonlinearity” slide. The resulting force balance includes the base damping contribution exactly once. Equivalent force symbols, damping-coefficient notation, algebraically equivalent expressions, and alternative subspace labels or conditions identifying the same physical contact regions are acceptable.

Includes the backlash-subspace figure on the “Backlash Nonlinearity” slide, built using native PowerPoint drawing elements. The figure includes the position axis $x$, velocity axis $\dot{x}$, subspace labels $V_1$, $V$ and $V_2$, clearance thresholds $-b$ and $b$ on the position axis, and two switching boundaries with vertical and slanted segments.
States the continuity condition as \(y(x_j;\, x_{j-1}, s_{j-1}) = s_j,\ j = 1,\dots,m-1\) on the "Simulation Method" slide.

States the transformed two-point boundary value problem boundary equation as \(P\,Y(0) + Q\,Y(1) = \beta\).

It shows the time vector; initial state, subspace and forcing phase; system-matrix selection; state calculation; subspace checking; and the decision whether the subspace has changed. The “no” branch leads to stopping. The “yes” branch leads to finding the switching time, calculating the new initial condition and updating the forcing phase, followed by a return to system-matrix selection.
